title: Correct public distribution verification after release publication
outOfScope: Changing the already published v0.5.43 Release, Tag, or assets
Changing release identity metadata for a future release
Weakening source, asset, checksum, SBOM, provenance, or installer verification

sources.reason: Current verifier compares historical release.json with the highest public tag and fails after a successful publication.
Public distribution verification commands and their intended lifecycle entry points.
WI-18 acceptance and process-issue record requiring post-publication evidence.
Published release evidence: public v0.5.43 is the highest tag and is not draft.

riskAssessment.reason: The verifier must distinguish historical repository metadata from published source-bound release evidence without weakening any release checks.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized completion of the remediation plan and the published release evidence is available for verification.

preReviewWarnings: Review that post-publication mode does not silently substitute local historical metadata for public source-bound evidence.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A dedicated post-publication verification command can validate the highest public release without treating historical release.json as the published identity.
The verifier still requires a non-draft public release, exact tag/source binding, release assets, checksums, SBOM, provenance, and installer behavior.
Regression tests cover both pre-publication historical/candidate mode and post-publication public-tag mode.
The release workflow validates the created immutable Tag and public metadata asset before publication.
WI-18 records the failed post-publication check, corrective change, published v0.5.43 evidence, and the verification result.
guidelines: Keep historical, candidate, and published release identities distinct.
Do not weaken source-bound, asset, checksum, SBOM, provenance, or installer gates.
Keep the correction limited to public release verification, metadata asset binding, and the Quick Install verification boundary.

intent.problem: After v0.5.43 was publicly published, make check-release-distribution failed because repository release.json intentionally remains the historical v0.5.42 metadata while the highest public tag is v0.5.43. This prevents the required post-publication evidence check from completing.
constraints: Do not rewrite historical release.json or alter the published v0.5.43 Release and Tag.
Do not reduce any fail-closed identity, asset, checksum, SBOM, provenance, or installer verification.
The corrective change must pass the complete Work Item lifecycle before WI-19 begins.
intent.rationale: Pre-publication verification and post-publication verification have different authoritative identities. An explicit post-publication path makes that boundary executable instead of conflating historical metadata with the public release.

rawUserRequest: The remediation plan must continue through every Work Item. If a process problem is found during WI-18 publication, record it, correct the process first, complete the full PR/merge/close/branch-cleanup lifecycle, and then continue.

declaredIntent.summary: Add an explicit post-publication verification path that treats the highest public source-bound release as authoritative while preserving the historical repository metadata and every existing fail-closed gate.

evidence: make check-release-distribution (failure recorded as WI-18 process issue)
tests/test_release_distribution.py public asset integrity and source binding cases
tests/test_release_distribution.py public release and draft-release rejection cases

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized serial execution of the remediation plan, including Makefile governance verification changes, with no gate bypass.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
